title: Jasmonic Acid Oxidase (JAO): Balancing growth and defense in rice
content: Jasmonates play a central role in balancing plant growth and defense, being involved from germination and development to different stress responses (Campos et al. 2014; Guo et al. 2018; Ali and Baek 2020; Raza et al. 2020). Jasmonic acid (JA) is converted into different metabolites, such as methyl jasmonate, jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile), and 12-hydroxyjasmonic acid (Yang et al. 2019). JA-Ile is the bioactive form that mediates protein interactions in signaling processes, fine-tuning jasmonates in different organs or physiological situations (Widemann et al. 2013; Heitz et al. 2019). In Arabidopsis, 4 JASMONIC ACID OXIDASES (JAO) are involved in JA hydroxylation, which produces 12-hydroxyjasmonic acid. Notably, disruption of AtJAO2 redirects the metabolic flux toward JA-Ile, leading to constitutive JA-Ile–directed responses and fungi resistance (Smirnova et al. 2017).
